title: Fit keycaps to a keyboard row by a layout card
instruction: Fit the four keycaps onto the four switches in the color order shown on the white card, pressing each one fully down, and keep the keyboard plate where it is.
context: Keyboard, macropad and input-device assembly: matching keycaps to a layout and pressing them onto their switches while the other hand keeps the loose plate from sliding.
setup: A wooden table; all positions are from the midpoint between the two arm bases, measured forward and toward the left arm. A loose aluminum keyboard plate section (300 x 45 x 15 mm, 0.25 kg, dark gray) lies flat with its center 330 mm forward and 30 mm toward the left arm, its long side parallel to the line between the arm bases. Four MX-style switches (gray 14 x 14 mm housings, 6 mm tall above the plate) stand in a row along the plate, 27 mm apart center to center, the group centered 125 mm toward the left arm. A white card (115 x 30 mm) lies flat 400 mm forward with four 12 mm color squares lined up with the switches: red, green, blue, yellow, from the left arm's side. Four solid-color ABS keycaps (18 x 18 x 10 mm) stand upright on the table 250 mm forward, in a row 35 mm apart: blue 200 mm toward the left arm, then yellow, red and green.
scoring: Per keycap: 0.25 if it sits flat on the switch whose card square has its color (within 1.5 mm of its seated height) and centered within 3 mm of that switch; 0.1 if it rests on that switch, centered within 6 mm, but is tilted or further off center; 0 if it is on another switch, off its switch or on the table. The score is the sum (1.0 at most). If the plate ends more than 10 mm from where it started, the score is capped at 0.5. Success (1.0) once all four are seated with the plate in place and the keycaps still for 1 s.
reset_notes: Pull the keycaps off with a keycap puller; return the plate and keycaps to their start positions (tape marks).
fidelity: Rigid boxes for the plate, switches, keycaps and card. The switch stems are not modeled: a keycap counts as pressed down once it sits flat on its housing, and the 3 mm centering tolerance stands in for the stem guiding a real keycap into place. The switches are fixed to the table while the plate is a separate loose body, so a plate pushed out from under them leaves them in place (the score is capped once the plate moves more than 10 mm). The switches are 27 mm apart rather than the 19.05 mm of a standard keyboard, because the YAM fingertips reach about 13 mm to each side of a gripped keycap and would land on a neighbouring keycap at the standard pitch. Keycaps weigh 30 g in simulation (about 4 g in reality) to keep the finger contacts stable. Color squares stand in for printed legends.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0 (step limit reached, no keycap seated); demo: 1.0
